topic: Three mat Pilates exercises to do at home

slides.headline: No reformer? Try these three on the mat
slides.sub: Three simple Pilates exercises you can do at home with just a mat.

slides.title: 1. Bridge
slides.body: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Breathe out and lift your hips until your body makes a line from shoulders to knees. Lower slowly. Try 8 to 10 reps.

slides.title: 2. Dead bug
slides.body: Lie on your back with knees and arms up. Slowly lower one arm and the opposite leg towards the floor, keeping your lower back relaxed, then return. Alternate sides for 8 to 10 reps.

slides.title: 3. Side-lying clam
slides.body: Lie on your side, knees bent, heels together. Keep your feet touching and lift the top knee without rolling your hips back. Lower slowly. Try 10 to 12 reps each side.

slides.title: How to fit them in
slides.body: Do one to two rounds, three or so times a week. Move slowly and breathe steadily. The goal is smooth control, not speed. Pick a regular spot in your day, like before dinner.

slides.title: Check with us first if
slides.body: You're recovering from an injury or surgery, you're pregnant, or any exercise causes sharp pain or pain that lingers into the next day. We can adjust the moves to suit you.

slides.headline: Want these tailored to you?
slides.body: Our Pilates team at Hybrid Physiotherapy can check your technique and adjust these exercises to your body and goals.

caption:
No reformer at home? No problem. A mat and ten minutes is enough to get started.

Three simple moves to try: bridges for your glutes and back of the legs, dead bugs for control through your trunk, and side-lying clams for the side of your hips. Move slowly, breathe steadily and aim for smooth control rather than speed. One or two rounds, a few times a week, is a good starting point.

If you're recovering from an injury or surgery, you're pregnant, or anything causes sharp or lingering pain, check with us first so we can adjust the exercises.
